rics.description: BIS, Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
rics.meaning: BIS Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index — comprehensive USD strength gauge against ~60 trading partners. Bank for International Settlements.
rics.how_to_use: Broader than Fed TWI; methodologically different weights. Use as cross-check on Fed series. BIS series has the longest cross-country history.

rics.description: BIS, Nominal Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index
rics.meaning: Nominal Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index — narrower basket (~26 advanced economies).
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner read on G10 USD positioning. Less noise from EM volatility.

rics.description: BIS, Real Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
rics.meaning: Real (CPI-adjusted) Broad Effective Exchange Rate. Captures real competitiveness.
rics.how_to_use: True purchasing power gauge. Rising real EER = US loses real competitiveness even if nominal rate flat.

rics.description: BIS, Real Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside the broad index. Narrow vs broad gap = EM vs DM USD strength.

rics.meaning: USD/EUR exchange rate — noon NY fixing. The most-traded FX pair globally.
rics.how_to_use: Largest weight in trade-weighted USD (~25%). EUR strength typically reflects relative ECB-Fed policy stance + relative growth. EUR is a low-beta currency in risk-off (counterintuitively).

rics.meaning: Commercial Paper rate — short-term corporate borrowing.
rics.how_to_use: Front-end credit gauge. Spread to T-bills (CP-bill spread) widens in stress.

rics.description: Federal Reserve, Price-adjusted Trade Weighted Exchange Real Index Major Currencies
rics.meaning: Fed Trade Weighted Real Index — Major Currencies.
rics.how_to_use: Fed's own real USD index. Diverges slightly from BIS due to weighting methodology.

rics.description: Federal Reserve, Real Advanced Foreign Economies Dollar Index
rics.meaning: Fed Real Advanced Foreign Economies Dollar Index.
rics.how_to_use: Newer Fed index focused on AE trading partners — successor to the Major Currencies index.

rics.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal USD MoM % change, standardized.
rics.how_to_use: High-frequency USD strength signal. Watch alongside DXY.

rics.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal USD YoY % change. The most market-relevant USD strength gauge for cycle-cycle comparisons.
rics.how_to_use: >5% YoY USD strength is historically a drag on US multinational EPS (S&P 500 derives ~40% of revenue overseas). Triggers translation hedging activity in corporate treasury.

rics.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, Standardized
rics.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal US dollar index, standardized — Fed's broad USD strength gauge against major + emerging trading partners. Refinitiv/LSEG version.
rics.how_to_use: Rising = stronger USD = headwind for US exporters and EM debt service. Sub-components: USD vs DM (G10) vs USD vs EM. ~50% weight is EUR/CNY/JPY/MXN/CAD combined.

rics.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.how_to_use: Strips inflation differentials. Cleaner competitiveness signal than nominal.

rics.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.how_to_use: Best annual USD competitiveness measure for trade modeling.

rics.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, Standardized
rics.meaning: Trade-weighted REAL USD index (CPI-adjusted) — strips inflation differentials. The cleaner competitiveness signal.
rics.how_to_use: Diverges from nominal USD when inflation differs across trading partners. Real USD up while nominal flat = US loses real competitiveness even with stable nominal rate.

rics.description: Purchasing power parity, National currency per USD
rics.meaning: Purchasing power parity — units of national currency per USD. For US, this is base = 1.0.
rics.how_to_use: Useful only for cross-country GDP comparisons. Not market-tradable.
